Hi Tamas,

Thank you for reaching out and sharing your questions. I have outlined some
recommendations with screenshots below.

Summary of our best practices for more accurate annotation and object
tracking

   - *New SAM 3 Functionality* - I am excited to share that I've now
   enabled SAM 3 in your account. Sharing a summary video
   <https://www.loom.com/share/96259881c53b4426a898ad69af302e42> and our
   documentation
   <https://docs.encord.com/platform-documentation/Annotate/automated-labeling/annotate-sam3>
for
   more context - keen to hear how the new functionality works for your
   projects.
   - *SAM 2* - I'd suggest opting for drawing a slightly larger bounding
   box over the object vs. using the click the relevant segment approach, as
   the box prompt is more likely to identify the object outlines. Once you're
   happy with the initial segmentation, then utilise the tracking
   functionality.
   - *Leveraging Editor Settings* - enabling the advanced tracking toggle
   and you can decrease the value of the Segment Anything RDP parameter to
   increase tracking accuracy (see screenshots below).

Lastly, I’d like to note that an out-of-the-box model can offer efficiency
gains in annotation time. However, for more specialised objects such as
medical tools, some level of human input is still needed to achieve the
highest accuracy. Similarly, SAM performs best on higher-resolution files;
blurred frames can make it difficult for the model to detect object
boundaries automatically. When this occurs, you can always use the brush
and eraser tools to refine the annotations for optimal precision.

Kind regards,
Arisha
